claim: The card scrolls on a rubber band — linear through the middle, straining with resistance near the ends, twanging back when released.

q1_defects.answer: No broken/blank states. Idle, play-3, and all control frames keep the full ship-quality card (brass header, blue dot, 3 grey rows, rounded panel) crisp and well-framed. No clipping, no slab, no console/network errors.

q2_reads_as.answer: Reads as elastic rubber-band resistance: near the extreme the card strains and elongates (resistance-high and elasticity-high pull it taller, ovalizing the accent dot), and play-3 shows it twanged up to a higher position vs the strained idle. The 'strain near the ends, twang back when released' claim is legible.

q3_discoverable.answer: All three labeled controls change the frame sensibly: 'Resistance' increases the strain/stretch near the extreme (low = squarer/lower, high = taller/higher), 'elasticity' increases the elastic elongation/twang, and 'span' adjusts the travel range. A user dragging any slider feels the band respond.

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive: play deltas 5.35/11.96/8.32 show motion and all 3 controls are live with monotonic luma/banding progressions (resistance luma 16.4->17.9, elasticity luma 16.4->18.6). No dead controls.
evidence: metrics: play-1 delta=5.35 play-2 delta=11.96 play-3 delta=8.32

q5_net.answer: A user would be PLEASED: 'it pulls tight and strains when I push it to the edge, then twangs back like a rubber band' — the elastic resistance reads, the card stays pristine, and every slider does something.

flags.note: The strain/elongation read is a vertical stretch similar to the velocity-stretch tile; a touch of audible-feeling overshoot wobble at release would differentiate the 'twang' more from a plain stretch. Pure taste.
